rights.scope: Amphora-authored compilation of closed-form Scheffe simplex-design point/term counts (published closed forms, not copied tables) plus Amphora-authored marine epoxy-amine constrained-mixture component-bound regions, for AUDIT_ONLY mixture-geometry oracles.

primary_sources.citation: Scheffe, H. (1958) 'Experiments with Mixtures', Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B 20(2):344-360.
primary_sources.supplies: Simplex-lattice design {q,m}; point count C(q+m-1, m); canonical (Scheffe) polynomial form and its term count; saturation of {q,m} for the degree-m canonical polynomial.

primary_sources.citation: Scheffe, H. (1963) 'The Simplex-Centroid Design for Experiments with Mixtures', Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B 25(2):235-263.
McLean, R.A. and Anderson, V.L. (1966) 'Extreme Vertices Design of Mixture Experiments', Technometrics 8(3):447-454.
primary_sources.supplies: Extreme-vertices generation for a constrained mixture region with lower and upper component bounds: set q-1 components to bound levels, fill the remaining component by difference, discard out-of-bound fills.

primary_sources.citation: Snee, R.D. and Marquardt, D.W. (1974) 'Extreme Vertices Designs for Linear Mixture Models', Technometrics 16(3):399-408.
primary_sources.supplies: Caveat that the McLean-Anderson generator emits candidate points that are not extreme vertices of the constrained region, so a screening step is required.

primary_sources.citation: Piepel, G.F. (1983) 'Defining Consistent Constraint Regions in Mixture Experiments', Technometrics 25(1):97-101.
primary_sources.supplies: Consistency predicate sum(l) <= 1 <= sum(u) for a non-empty constrained mixture region, and the implied (consistent) bounds l*_i = max(l_i, 1 - sum_{j!=i} u_j), u*_i = min(u_i, 1 - sum_{j!=i} l_j), which equal the exact attainable range of x_i over the region.

primary_sources.citation: Motzkin, T.S., Raiffa, H., Thompson, G.L., Thrall, R.M. (1953) 'The Double Description Method', in Contributions to the Theory of Games Vol. II, Annals of Mathematics Studies 28, Princeton University Press, pp. 51-73.
primary_sources.supplies: Independent (cut-the-simplex) vertex enumeration path used as the parity oracle against the McLean-Anderson generator.

primary_sources.citation: Cornell, J.A. (2002) 'Experiments with Mixtures: Designs, Models, and the Analysis of Mixture Data', 3rd ed., Wiley.
primary_sources.supplies: Textbook consolidation of the above closed forms (simplex-lattice, simplex-centroid, special-cubic term count q + C(q,2) + C(q,3)).

closed_form_anchors.note: Values below are evaluated from the published closed forms, independently re-derived by brute-force enumeration in the harness. They are closed-form evaluations, not reproductions of copyrighted tables.

coating_mixture_regions.industrial_context: Marine anti-corrosion two-part epoxy-amine primer, weight fractions of the mixed (A+B) wet paint.
High-build glass-flake barrier topcoat over epoxy primer, weight fractions of the mixed wet paint.
Solvent-free epoxy-amine ballast/cargo tank lining, weight fractions of the mixed wet coating.
Deliberately loose declared upper bounds on a 4-component epoxy-amine primer; exercises Piepel 1983 upper implied-bound tightening.
Narrow-window tank-lining region with sum(upper) only slightly above 1; exercises Piepel 1983 lower implied-bound tightening.
Fully specified epoxy-amine lining where sum(lower) == 1 exactly; the constrained region collapses to one point.

cartesian_closure_cases.note: Uniform 1/m grid on each of q composition axes: (m+1)^q mixed-radix Cartesian points, of which exactly C(q+m-1, m) satisfy the closure constraint sum(x) = 1.
